heroHeadline: Machado Announces Presidential Run as Trump Administration Shields Rodríguez from Prosecution
heroSubtitle: Nobel laureate María Corina Machado announced from Panama on May 23 that she will run for Venezuela's presidency and plans to return from exile by end-2026, while simultaneously signaling openness to election negotiations with Acting President Delcy Rodríguez's transitional government. On May 27, the Trump administration directed federal prosecutors not to pursue criminal probes of Rodríguez — a longtime DEA drug trafficking target — drawing criticism from Democratic senators and human rights groups who argue the US is prioritizing oil access over democratic accountability. ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips began negotiations on May 26 for a potential return to Venezuela's oil sector, and US Marines conducted a rapid response exercise at the reopened Caracas embassy. Venezuela also freed its three longest-held political prisoners on May 24 — Erasmo Bolívar, Héctor Rovaín, and Luis Molina — jailed for 23 years since the 2002 coup.
